annotations.title: Preview a CSV before importing it

tools.description: Preview a CSV before importing it. Command `data.preview`. Reads CSV text without storing anything and returns every admissible reading of it: each delimiter (comma, semicolon, tab) with each decimal mark that gives a numeric time column and a numeric concentration column, with the columns, the first rows, what was guessed and the checks on the result (time going back, duplicated times). The first reading is recommended. `needs_choice` is true when the file can be read more than one way or the recommended reading has failed checks: the caller should show the readings and let the person choose, then pass the chosen `delimiter` and `decimal_comma` to data.import. Nothing is imported.

rows.description: Rows of each reading to return; at most 200 (a larger number is capped at 200).

tools.name: data_preview
tools.title: Preview a CSV before importing it

annotations.title: Import a CSV into a new worksheet

tools.description: Import a CSV into a new worksheet. Command `data.import`. Reads CSV text (header line, one line per row; comma, semicolon or tab; a decimal comma is understood with a semicolon) into a new worksheet. Roles (time, concentration, subject, dose, route) and units written in the headers, such as `Conc (ng/mL)`, are recognised; `notes` lists what was guessed or ignored. Use `columns` to set a role or a unit explicitly.

columns.description: Explicit role or unit for named columns; a null unit clears it.

tools.name: data_import

tools.description: Run a non-compartmental analysis. Command `nca.run`. Runs the NCA on the profiles of a worksheet (one subject, or all) and stores the result in an analysis object (new, or `analysis` updated). Each subject gives its parameters by PKNCA name, each a value or `not_calculated` with a reason, or an error saying what to fix. The route and dose come from the arguments or from the route and dose columns.

Id.description: Identifier of a worksheet or an analysis, as returned by the command that created it.

NcaOptions.description: Conventions of the NCA; every field is optional and defaults to the documented value.

anyOf.description: Units of time, concentration (mass/volume: ng, µg (ug, mcg), mg, g per mL or L) and dose (a mass). Results then carry a unit each; CL and volumes are in L. Absent: unitless results, flagged units_missing.

analysis.description: Update and re-run this analysis instead of creating a new one.

subject.description: One subject, a label as text or number; omitted or null: every subject (NCA) or the only subject (fit).

tools.name: nca_run

tools.description: Initial estimates from the data. Command `fit.initial_estimates`. Estimates the starting values of a model's parameters from one subject's profile (log-linear regression, curve stripping, terminal phase). Reads only: nothing is stored. A zero-order input model needs its duration among `fixed`. Refused for pk2: give the initial values.

Id.description: Identifier of a worksheet or an analysis, as returned by the command that created it.

ModelId.description: Route and input. pk1: v and cl or k. pk2 (two compartments): one set of cl,vc,q,vp or k10,k12,k21,vc or a,b,alpha,beta (a, b need the dose).

tools.description: Objective at the starting values. Command `fit.evaluate`. The weighted sum of squares of one subject's observations for the given starting values (or the generated ones when none are given), as the first row of a fit's trace. Reads only: nothing is stored. A page uses it to show how far the starting curve is from the data while the person edits the estimates.

FitOptions.description: Options of the fit; every field is optional and defaults to the documented value.

Id.description: Identifier of a worksheet or an analysis, as returned by the command that created it.

ModelId.description: Route and input. pk1: v and cl or k. pk2 (two compartments): one set of cl,vc,q,vp or k10,k12,k21,vc or a,b,alpha,beta (a, b need the dose).

initial.description: Initial estimates by parameter name; the fitted parameters are exactly those named. Empty: generated from the data (not for pk2: give every parameter).

annotations.title: Fit a model to a profile

tools.description: Fit a model to a profile. Command `fit.run`. Weighted least-squares fit (Gauss-Newton with the Levenberg and Hartley modification) of a one- or two-compartment model to the profile of one subject; stores the result in an analysis object. The result has the status (converged or why not), estimates with standard error, CV% and confidence intervals, diagnostics, observed and predicted values, the smooth curve, the trace, and quality flags. A fit that cannot start is an error and stores nothing.

FitOptions.description: Options of the fit; every field is optional and defaults to the documented value.

Id.description: Identifier of a worksheet or an analysis, as returned by the command that created it.

ModelId.description: Route and input. pk1: v and cl or k. pk2 (two compartments): one set of cl,vc,q,vp or k10,k12,k21,vc or a,b,alpha,beta (a, b need the dose).

analysis.description: Update and re-run this analysis instead of creating a new one.

initial.description: Initial estimates by parameter name; the fitted parameters are exactly those named. Empty: generated from the data (not for pk2: give every parameter).

subject.description: One subject, a label as text or number; omitted or null: every subject (NCA) or the only subject (fit).

tools.name: fit_run

Id.description: Identifier of a worksheet or an analysis, as returned by the command that created it.

annotations.title: Evaluate a model on a time grid

tools.description: Evaluate a model on a time grid. Command `model.simulate`. Concentration and AUC of a one- or two-compartment model at the given times (a list, or a regular grid), and its secondary parameters (half-life, clearance, AUC to infinity, MRT, predicted Cmax and Tmax...). Nothing is stored unless `store` is true (with `analysis`, that simulation is updated instead of a new one being created), so it can be called at every change of a parameter for a live curve.

Id.description: Identifier of a worksheet or an analysis, as returned by the command that created it.

ModelId.description: Route and input. pk1: v and cl or k. pk2 (two compartments): one set of cl,vc,q,vp or k10,k12,k21,vc or a,b,alpha,beta (a, b need the dose).

analysis.description: With `store`: update and re-run this simulation instead of creating a new one.

params.description: Parameters by name: pk1 `v` and one of `cl`, `k`; pk2 one set (see model); `ka`, `dur`, `tlag` as needed.

tools.name: model_simulate

Id.description: Identifier of a worksheet or an analysis, as returned by the command that created it.

tools.description: Load a project. Command `project.load`. Replaces the current project by a saved one, given as the document (`project`) or its JSON text (`text`). The file is checked first; a refused file changes nothing. The history saved with the project is adopted when this session has none yet (`history_restored`), so a project keeps its provenance across sessions; a session that already has a history keeps it, and loading is one more entry.
